statementSummary: I build and evaluate AI systems that must work reliably outside the lab. My work spans a deployed real-time traffic perception system (YOLOv8 with multi-object tracking), LLM-based applications and multi-agent pipelines. I am interested in how to measure whether such systems can be trusted: how detection errors propagate into decisions, how efficiently models can run on modest hardware, and when LLM agents and vision-language models can replace or complement purpose-built pipelines in low-resource, heterogeneous settings.

fypDetails.title: Real-Time Traffic Choking Point Detector
fypDetails.status: Final Year Project, NUML Islamabad (completed 2026). Held-out evaluation and a vision-language-model comparison are in progress.
fypDetails.abstract: We present a real-time congestion monitoring system deployed at two junctions in Islamabad (NUML Gate and 7-Up Chowk). A YOLOv8n detector, fine-tuned from COCO-pretrained weights on a self-collected four-class dataset (vehicle, bus, human, traffic controller), is combined with ByteTrack tracking and count-based congestion rules. Alerts are delivered through a FastAPI backend, a React dashboard and SMS. On the validation split the detector reaches mAP@50 of 89.5% and mAP@50-95 of 59.3%, with precision 86.4% and recall 84.7%, and runs at 3.1 ms per frame inference on [VERIFY: GPU model and image size]. End-to-end throughput is [VERIFY: 20-25 FPS as stated in the report, with hardware]. Error analysis shows that the vehicle class is over-counted at the default confidence threshold and that the human class has low precision, so we treat the current thresholds as a baseline for learned, better-calibrated congestion estimation.

results.split: Validation split (also used to select the best epoch). An independent held-out test set is in preparation.
results.efficiency: 3.1 ms/frame inference, 6.3 MB model. [VERIFY: GPU model, image size, and what the 3.1 ms includes.]
results.training: 282 epochs (best epoch 232), about 2.7 hours, COCO-pretrained initialization.

limitations: Metrics are from the validation split; an independent test set from different days or viewpoints is still needed.
At the confusion-matrix threshold, vehicle predictions exceed ground truth by roughly 23%, and the human class has low precision (many false positives, possibly unlabeled objects).
Congestion is decided by a fixed vehicle-count threshold rather than learned from speed, occupancy or stop duration.
Data come from two junctions, so cross-site generalization is untested.
All vehicle types are merged into a single class.

openQuestions: How do per-frame detection errors, such as the observed vehicle over-counting, propagate into congestion-state decisions, and can tracker-derived features (occupancy, speed, stop duration) replace fixed count thresholds?
When can open-weight vision-language models complement or replace a fine-tuned detector for congestion-state classification in heterogeneous traffic, and at what latency and cost?
How do multi-agent LLM pipelines compare with single-prompt baselines on citation correctness and unsupported claims?
How can the groundedness of retrieval-augmented health and nutrition assistants be measured, and how often do they produce unsupported claims compared with a no-retrieval baseline?
